# Fermentation

Bread and cheese are both fermented: microbes eat sugars and leave acids and gases behind. In a [[Sourdough levain]] wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria raise and sour the dough during [[Proofing dough]]; in cheese, [[Cheese cultures]] sour the milk before [[Rennet and curds]], and keep working while [[Aging cheese in a cave]]. Temperature sets the pace of both, which is why a [[Kneading and gluten|dough]] and a [[Brining feta|feta]] both slow down in the fridge.
